<div class="wp-block-coblocks-accordion">
<div class="wp-block-coblocks-accordion-item"><details><summary class="wp-block-coblocks-accordion-item__title has-background has-text-color has-white-color" style="background-color:#006e8d">What is the role of the Monitors</summary><div class="wp-block-coblocks-accordion-item__content" style="border-color:#006e8d">
<p>The Monitors are a neutral third-party appointed by the court to oversee and assess KCSO and the County’s progress in implementing, and achieving compliance with, the Stipulated Judgment. They report the status of implementation to the Parties and the Court and work with the Parties to address any barriers to compliance, as well as assist the Parties to informally resolve disputes or differences should they emerge. The Monitors shall not, and are not intended to, replace or assume the role and duties of the Sheriff or of the DOJ.</p>
</div></details></div>



<div class="wp-block-coblocks-accordion-item"><details><summary class="wp-block-coblocks-accordion-item__title has-background has-text-color has-white-color" style="background-color:#006e8d">How can I contact the Monitors with a question or concern?</summary><div class="wp-block-coblocks-accordion-item__content" style="border-color:#006e8d">
<p>Inquiries and concerns can be sent to the monitors from the <a href="https://kcsomonitoring.info/about-kcso-monitoring/contact-the-monitors/">Contact the Monitors</a> page.</p>
</div></details></div>



<div class="wp-block-coblocks-accordion-item"><details><summary class="wp-block-coblocks-accordion-item__title has-background has-text-color has-white-color" style="background-color:#006e8d">How do I make an inquiry or send a question to the Sheriff’s Office?</summary><div class="wp-block-coblocks-accordion-item__content" style="border-color:#006e8d">
<p>Inquiries and questions can be sent to the Kern County Sheriff’s Office <a href="https://www.kernsheriff.org/Contact">here</a>.</p>
</div></details></div>



<div class="wp-block-coblocks-accordion-item"><details><summary class="wp-block-coblocks-accordion-item__title has-background has-text-color has-white-color" style="background-color:#006e8d">How do I share a comment or complaint about the Sheriff’s Office?</summary><div class="wp-block-coblocks-accordion-item__content" style="border-color:#006e8d">
<p>Comments and complaints regarding the Sheriff’s Office need to be submitted directly to KCSO on a Complaint Form.</p>



<p>This can be done in person at a station, at various community locations such as public libraries, or online.</p>



<p>For more information, click on the following links:</p>



<p><a href="https://www.kernsheriff.org/Internal_Affairs" target="_blank" rel="noreferrer noopener">Internal Affairs | KCSO (kernsheriff.org)</a></p>



<p><a href="https://www.kernsheriff.org/Complaints_Document/citizen_complaint_brochure.pdf" target="_blank" rel="noreferrer noopener">Document/citizen_complaint_brochure.pdf</a></p>



<p><a href="https://www.kernsheriff.org/Complaints_Document/Public_Complaint_Brochure-August_2023.pdf" target="_blank" rel="noreferrer noopener">Online personnel complaint form in English</a></p>



<p><a href="https://www.kernsheriff.org/Complaints_Document/Public%20Complaint%20Brochure.ES.pdf" target="_blank" rel="noreferrer noopener">Online personnel complaint form in Spanish</a></p>



<p><a href="https://www.kernsheriff.org/complaints" target="_blank" rel="noreferrer noopener">Process on How to Submit a Complaint</a></p>
</div></details></div>



<div class="wp-block-coblocks-accordion-item"><details><summary class="wp-block-coblocks-accordion-item__title has-background has-text-color has-white-color" style="background-color:#006e8d">What is the Communitywide Advisory Council (CAC) and how can I learn more about it?</summary><div class="wp-block-coblocks-accordion-item__content" style="border-color:#006e8d">
<p>The KCSO Communitywide Advisory Council (CAC) was established as part of the stipulated judgment. The CAC is a diverse group of Kern County residents advocating for positive change in relations, policies, and laws to create a safer community. CAC meetings are open to the public (see the <a href="https://kcsomonitoring.info/news-events/">News & Events</a> page) via Zoom, and focus on the eight key areas of reforms and objectives to be met by KCSO, as identified in the stipulated judgment. To learn more about the CAC, visit <a href="https://kerncac.org/" target="_blank" rel="noreferrer noopener">https://kerncac.org</a>.</p>
</div></details></div>



<div class="wp-block-coblocks-accordion-item"><details><summary class="wp-block-coblocks-accordion-item__title has-background has-text-color has-white-color" style="background-color:#006e8d">How do I submit a complaint against the County of Kern?</summary><div class="wp-block-coblocks-accordion-item__content" style="border-color:#006e8d">
<p><a href="https://www.kernsheriff.org/complaints" target="_blank" rel="noreferrer noopener">Claim Against the County of Kern</a></p>
</div></details></div>
</div>

					<div class="elementor-column elementor-col-100 elementor-top-column elementor-element elementor-element-2ac77bbe" data-id="2ac77bbe" data-element_type="column">
			<div class="elementor-widget-wrap elementor-element-populated">
						<div class="elementor-element elementor-element-13e35a09 elementor-widget elementor-widget-text-editor" data-id="13e35a09" data-element_type="widget" data-widget_type="text-editor.default">
				<div class="elementor-widget-container">
									
<h4>The Stipulated Judgment</h4>
<p>The Stipulated Judgment specifically identifies eight key areas of reforms and objectives to be met by KCSO, which are briefly summarized here. Please see the <a href="https://oag.ca.gov/sites/default/files/Judgment.pdf" data-type="URL" data-id="https://oag.ca.gov/sites/default/files/Judgment.pdf">full judgment</a> for exact wording and details.</p>
<div class="ewd-ufaq-faq-list ewd-ufaq-page-type-distinct ewd-ufaq-category-tabs-" id="ewd-ufaq-faq-list">
<p>	<input type="hidden" name="show_on_load" value="" id="ewd-ufaq-show-on-load"><br>
<input type="hidden" name="include_category" value="" id="ewd-ufaq-include-category"><br>
<input type="hidden" name="exclude_category" value="" id="ewd-ufaq-exclude-category"><br>
<input type="hidden" name="orderby" value="title" id="ewd-ufaq-orderby"><br>
<input type="hidden" name="order" value="asc" id="ewd-ufaq-order"><br>
<input type="hidden" name="post_count" value="-1" id="ewd-ufaq-post-count"><br>
<input type="hidden" name="current_url" value="/" id="ewd-ufaq-current-url"></p>
<div class="ewd-ufaq-faqs">
<div id="ewd-ufaq-faq-category-judgement-details" class="ewd-ufaq-faq-category">
<div class="ewd-ufaq-faq-category-title ">
<h3 title="Click here to open Key Judgment Sections">
			Key Judgment Sections					</h3>
<p></p></div>
<div class="ewd-ufaq-faq-category-inner ">
<div class="ewd-ufaq-faq-div ewd-ufaq-faq-column-count-one ewd-ufaq-faq-responsive-columns- ewd-ufaq-faq-display-style-default ewd-ufaq-can-be-toggled" id="ewd-ufaq-post-137-cX64ds5AMI" data-post_id="137">
<div class="ewd-ufaq-faq-title ewd-ufaq-faq-toggle">
<p>	<a class="ewd-ufaq-post-margin" href="#" role="button"></a></p><a class="ewd-ufaq-post-margin" href="#" role="button">
<div class="ewd-ufaq-post-margin-symbol ewd-ufaq-">
			<span>a</span>
		</div>
<div class="ewd-ufaq-faq-title-text">
<h4>
				1. Use of Force			</h4>
<p></p></div>
<div class="ewd-ufaq-clear"></div>
</a><p><a class="ewd-ufaq-post-margin" href="#" role="button">	</a></p>
</div>
<div class="ewd-ufaq-faq-body ewd-ufaq-hidden">
<div class="ewd-ufaq-post-margin ewd-ufaq-faq-post">
<p>KCSO agrees to revise its use of force policies and practices in accordance with both federal and state constitutions; federal and state laws; and to include the concepts of sanctity of life, necessity, proportionality, and de-escalation. Deputies shall receive training on all new and updated policies. KCSO deputies and staff will use force only when necessary to defend against an imminent threat of death or serious bodily injury; when feasible, they will use de-escalation techniques, crisis intervention tactics, and other alternatives. The KCSO shall:</p>
<p>• Have an affirmative duty to intervene when another deputy/employee is about to use, or is using, unnecessary or excessive force;<br>• Require deputies to report all uses of force greater than an authorized control hold;<br>• Develop a strategic plan to meaningfully engage with the community and work with the CAC in developing the revised use of force policies;<br>• Develop a policy and process to inform the public about all officer involved shootings, deaths in custody;<br>• Prohibit chokeholds, carotid restrains, and other such maneuvers;<br>• Revise its canine-related policies and training;<br>• Mandate reportable uses of force to be investigated by supervisors; and, <br>• Use data to identify concerning trends and to identify and correct deficiencies revealed by analysis.</p>
<p>(Please see the <a href="https://oag.ca.gov/sites/default/files/Judgment.pdf">full agreement</a> for exact wording and details.)</p>
</div></div>
</div>
<div class="ewd-ufaq-faq-div ewd-ufaq-faq-column-count-one ewd-ufaq-faq-responsive-columns- ewd-ufaq-faq-display-style-default ewd-ufaq-can-be-toggled" id="ewd-ufaq-post-136-bRleAGBArI" data-post_id="136">
<div class="ewd-ufaq-faq-title ewd-ufaq-faq-toggle">
<p>	<a class="ewd-ufaq-post-margin" href="#" role="button"></a></p><a class="ewd-ufaq-post-margin" href="#" role="button">
<div class="ewd-ufaq-post-margin-symbol ewd-ufaq-">
			<span>a</span>
		</div>
<div class="ewd-ufaq-faq-title-text">
<h4>
				2. Stops, Seizures, and Searches			</h4>
<p></p></div>
<div class="ewd-ufaq-clear"></div>
</a><p><a class="ewd-ufaq-post-margin" href="#" role="button">	</a></p>
</div>
<div class="ewd-ufaq-faq-body ewd-ufaq-hidden">
<div class="ewd-ufaq-post-margin ewd-ufaq-faq-post">
<p>KCSO agrees to ensure that all investigatory stops, seizures, and searches are conducted in accordance with federal and state constitutions. All investigatory stops will be adequately documented for tracking and supervision purposes. KCSO shall provide training on bias-free policing and implement additional accountability and supervision practices to ensure that unlawful stops, searches, and seizures are detected and effectively addressed. KCSO will work with the Monitor on a semiannual basis to analyze its stop data and revise policies and trainings as warranted.</p>
<p>(Please see the <a href="https://oag.ca.gov/sites/default/files/Judgment.pdf">full agreement</a> for exact wording and details.)</p>
<p></p>
</div></div>
</div>
<div class="ewd-ufaq-faq-div ewd-ufaq-faq-column-count-one ewd-ufaq-faq-responsive-columns- ewd-ufaq-faq-display-style-default ewd-ufaq-can-be-toggled" id="ewd-ufaq-post-193-yyvGODlZDz" data-post_id="193">
<div class="ewd-ufaq-faq-title ewd-ufaq-faq-toggle">
<p>	<a class="ewd-ufaq-post-margin" href="#" role="button"></a></p><a class="ewd-ufaq-post-margin" href="#" role="button">
<div class="ewd-ufaq-post-margin-symbol ewd-ufaq-">
			<span>a</span>
		</div>
<div class="ewd-ufaq-faq-title-text">
<h4>
				3. Responding to and Interacting With People With Behavioral Health Disparities or in Crisis			</h4>
<p></p></div>
<div class="ewd-ufaq-clear"></div>
</a><p><a class="ewd-ufaq-post-margin" href="#" role="button">	</a></p>
</div>
<div class="ewd-ufaq-faq-body ewd-ufaq-hidden">
<div class="ewd-ufaq-post-margin ewd-ufaq-faq-post">
<p>KCSO shall revise its policies to establish that deputies who are specifically trained in de-escalation techniques be dispatched to respond to calls involving a person in mental health crisis or suffering from a mental health disability. KCSO shall ensure deputies are equipped with methods to properly interact with this community, to reduce the number of individuals with behavioral health disabilities in the criminal justice system.</p>
<p>(Please see the <a href="https://oag.ca.gov/sites/default/files/Judgment.pdf">full agreement</a> for exact wording and details.)</p>
</div></div>
</div>
<div class="ewd-ufaq-faq-div ewd-ufaq-faq-column-count-one ewd-ufaq-faq-responsive-columns- ewd-ufaq-faq-display-style-default ewd-ufaq-can-be-toggled" id="ewd-ufaq-post-194-hBfXGURwtY" data-post_id="194">
<div class="ewd-ufaq-faq-title ewd-ufaq-faq-toggle">
<p>	<a class="ewd-ufaq-post-margin" href="#" role="button"></a></p><a class="ewd-ufaq-post-margin" href="#" role="button">
<div class="ewd-ufaq-post-margin-symbol ewd-ufaq-">
			<span>a</span>
		</div>
<div class="ewd-ufaq-faq-title-text">
<h4>
				4. Management and Supervisory Oversight			</h4>
<p></p></div>
<div class="ewd-ufaq-clear"></div>
</a><p><a class="ewd-ufaq-post-margin" href="#" role="button">	</a></p>
</div>
<div class="ewd-ufaq-faq-body ewd-ufaq-hidden">
<div class="ewd-ufaq-post-margin ewd-ufaq-faq-post">
<p>KCSO will ensure all supervisors and managers exercise oversight of use of force incidents, conduct impartial investigations of those matters, are held accountable for meeting agency standards and expectations, engage with and listen to community feedback, and incorporate said feedback when able and appropriate. KCSO will develop specific metrics and guidelines for evaluating the effectiveness of the supervision of deputies and perform these evaluations annually.</p>
<p>(Please see the <a href="https://oag.ca.gov/sites/default/files/Judgment.pdf">full agreement</a> for exact wording and details.)</p>
</div></div>
</div>
<div class="ewd-ufaq-faq-div ewd-ufaq-faq-column-count-one ewd-ufaq-faq-responsive-columns- ewd-ufaq-faq-display-style-default ewd-ufaq-can-be-toggled" id="ewd-ufaq-post-195-PicM8MjIPK" data-post_id="195">
<div class="ewd-ufaq-faq-title ewd-ufaq-faq-toggle">
<p>	<a class="ewd-ufaq-post-margin" href="#" role="button"></a></p><a class="ewd-ufaq-post-margin" href="#" role="button">
<div class="ewd-ufaq-post-margin-symbol ewd-ufaq-">
			<span>a</span>
		</div>
<div class="ewd-ufaq-faq-title-text">
<h4>
				5. Language Access			</h4>
<p></p></div>
<div class="ewd-ufaq-clear"></div>
</a><p><a class="ewd-ufaq-post-margin" href="#" role="button">	</a></p>
</div>
<div class="ewd-ufaq-faq-body ewd-ufaq-hidden">
<div class="ewd-ufaq-post-margin ewd-ufaq-faq-post">
<p>KCSO will ensure that all members of the Kern County community, regardless of their ability to speak, read, write, or understand English, will be provided with timely and meaningful access to police services and with effective communication. KCSO agrees to partner with the CAC and community stakeholders to develop and implement a language access policy consistent with applicable federal and state laws. KCSO will develop and audit protocol to determine how it is managing language access services and whether the services align with community needs. Audit results will be reported annually to the public.</p>
<p>(Please see the <a href="https://oag.ca.gov/sites/default/files/Judgment.pdf">full agreement</a> for exact wording and details.)</p>
</div></div>
</div>
<div class="ewd-ufaq-faq-div ewd-ufaq-faq-column-count-one ewd-ufaq-faq-responsive-columns- ewd-ufaq-faq-display-style-default ewd-ufaq-can-be-toggled" id="ewd-ufaq-post-196-hd2bdKOrsD" data-post_id="196">
<div class="ewd-ufaq-faq-title ewd-ufaq-faq-toggle">
<p>	<a class="ewd-ufaq-post-margin" href="#" role="button"></a></p><a class="ewd-ufaq-post-margin" href="#" role="button">
<div class="ewd-ufaq-post-margin-symbol ewd-ufaq-">
			<span>a</span>
		</div>
<div class="ewd-ufaq-faq-title-text">
<h4>
				6. Recruitment, Hiring, and Promotions			</h4>
<p></p></div>
<div class="ewd-ufaq-clear"></div>
</a><p><a class="ewd-ufaq-post-margin" href="#" role="button">	</a></p>
</div>
<div class="ewd-ufaq-faq-body ewd-ufaq-hidden">
<div class="ewd-ufaq-post-margin ewd-ufaq-faq-post">
<p>KCSO will develop and implement plans and policies to ensure it successfully attracts and hires a diverse group of qualified individuals for both patrol and detentions. These shall be designed to ensure that recruitment, hiring, and promotion decisions are made without favoritism or unlawful discrimination and incorporate enhanced strategies for promoting qualified applicant representatives of the Kern County community. KCSO will report annually on their promotional activities and outcomes.</p>
<p>(Please see the <a href="https://oag.ca.gov/sites/default/files/Judgment.pdf">full agreement</a> for exact wording and details.)</p>
</div></div>
</div>
<div class="ewd-ufaq-faq-div ewd-ufaq-faq-column-count-one ewd-ufaq-faq-responsive-columns- ewd-ufaq-faq-display-style-default ewd-ufaq-can-be-toggled" id="ewd-ufaq-post-197-8qpli8hSKz" data-post_id="197">
<div class="ewd-ufaq-faq-title ewd-ufaq-faq-toggle">
<p>	<a class="ewd-ufaq-post-margin" href="#" role="button"></a></p><a class="ewd-ufaq-post-margin" href="#" role="button">
<div class="ewd-ufaq-post-margin-symbol ewd-ufaq-">
			<span>a</span>
		</div>
<div class="ewd-ufaq-faq-title-text">
<h4>
				7. Community Policing			</h4>
<p></p></div>
<div class="ewd-ufaq-clear"></div>
</a><p><a class="ewd-ufaq-post-margin" href="#" role="button">	</a></p>
</div>
<div class="ewd-ufaq-faq-body ewd-ufaq-hidden">
<div class="ewd-ufaq-post-margin ewd-ufaq-faq-post">
<p>KCSO agrees to enhance, promote, and strengthen partnerships within the community, to engage constructively with the community to ensure collaborative problem-solving and bias-free policing, and to increase transparency and community confidence in KCSO. To do this, KCSO will:<br>• Develop identified policies with input from the CAC and other community stakeholders;<br>• Create easy points of access for community feedback and input;<br>• Develop a plan to actively attend community meetings and events;<br>• Provide annual training on community policing and problem-oriented policing methods;<br>• Report annually on its community engagement efforts; and,<br>• Conduct a Community Survey with the assistance of the Monitoring Team.</p>
<p>(Please see the <a href="https://oag.ca.gov/sites/default/files/Judgment.pdf">full agreement</a> for exact wording and details.)</p>
</div></div>
</div>
<div class="ewd-ufaq-faq-div ewd-ufaq-faq-column-count-one ewd-ufaq-faq-responsive-columns- ewd-ufaq-faq-display-style-default ewd-ufaq-can-be-toggled" id="ewd-ufaq-post-198-RcBuyUwleG" data-post_id="198">
<div class="ewd-ufaq-faq-title ewd-ufaq-faq-toggle">
<p>	<a class="ewd-ufaq-post-margin" href="#" role="button"></a></p><a class="ewd-ufaq-post-margin" href="#" role="button">
<div class="ewd-ufaq-post-margin-symbol ewd-ufaq-">
			<span>a</span>
		</div>
<div class="ewd-ufaq-faq-title-text">
<h4>
				8. Personnel Complaint Review			</h4>
<p></p></div>
<div class="ewd-ufaq-clear"></div>
</a><p><a class="ewd-ufaq-post-margin" href="#" role="button">	</a></p>
</div>
<div class="ewd-ufaq-faq-body ewd-ufaq-hidden">
<div class="ewd-ufaq-post-margin ewd-ufaq-faq-post">
<p>KCSO will ensure that all allegations of personnel misconduct are received and fully and fairly investigated. Personnel who commit misconduct will be held accountable pursuant to a fair disciplinary system and consistent standards. All KCSO deputies and supervisors will receive training about proper complaint intake, classification, and investigative techniques. Audits of these practices will be conducted annually.</p>
<p>(Please see the <a href="https://oag.ca.gov/sites/default/files/Judgment.pdf" target="_blank" rel="noreferrer noopener">full agreement</a> for exact wording and details.)</p>
</div></div>
</div>
</div>
</div></div>
</div>

FAQs What is the role of the Monitors The Monitors are a neutral third-party appointed by the court to oversee and assess KCSO and the County’s progress in implementing, and achieving compliance with, the Stipulated Judgment. They report the status of implementation to the Parties and the Court and work with the Parties to address any barriers to compliance, as well as assist the Parties to informally resolve disputes or differences should they emerge. The Monitors shall not, and are not intended to, replace or assume the role and duties of the Sheriff or of the DOJ. How can I contact the Monitors with a question or concern? Inquiries and concerns can be sent to the monitors from the Contact the Monitors page. How do I make an inquiry or send a question to the Sheriff’s Office? Inquiries and questions can be sent to the Kern County Sheriff’s Office here. How do I share a comment or complaint about the Sheriff’s Office? Comments and complaints regarding the Sheriff’s Office need to be submitted directly to KCSO on a Complaint Form. This can be done in person at a station, at various community locations such as public libraries, or online. For more information, click on the following links: Internal Affairs | KCSO (kernsheriff.org) Document/citizen_complaint_brochure.pdf Online personnel complaint form in English Online personnel complaint form in Spanish Process on How to Submit a Complaint What is the Communitywide Advisory Council (CAC) and how can I learn more about it? The KCSO Communitywide Advisory Council (CAC) was established as part of the stipulated judgment. The CAC is a diverse group of Kern County residents advocating for positive change in relations, policies, and laws to create a safer community. CAC meetings are open to the public (see the News & Events page) via Zoom, and focus on the eight key areas of reforms and objectives to be met by KCSO, as identified in the stipulated judgment. To learn more about the CAC, visit https://kerncac.org. How do I submit a complaint against the County of Kern? Claim Against the County of Kern Important Links  Kern County Sheriff’s OfficeTransparency | KCSO (kernsheriff.org)Kern County, CAState of California, Department of Justice The Stipulated Judgment The Stipulated Judgment specifically identifies eight key areas of reforms and objectives to be met by KCSO, which are briefly summarized here. Please see the full judgment for exact wording and details. Key Judgment Sections a 1. Use of Force KCSO agrees to revise its use of force policies and practices in accordance with both federal and state constitutions; federal and state laws; and to include the concepts of sanctity of life, necessity, proportionality, and de-escalation. Deputies shall receive training on all new and updated policies. KCSO deputies and staff will use force only when necessary to defend against an imminent threat of death or serious bodily injury; when feasible, they will use de-escalation techniques, crisis intervention tactics, and other alternatives. The KCSO shall: • Have an affirmative duty to intervene when another deputy/employee is about to use, or is using, unnecessary or excessive force;• Require deputies to report all uses of force greater than an authorized control hold;• Develop a strategic plan to meaningfully engage with the community and work with the CAC in developing the revised use of force policies;• Develop a policy and process to inform the public about all officer involved shootings, deaths in custody;• Prohibit chokeholds, carotid restrains, and other such maneuvers;• Revise its canine-related policies and training;• Mandate reportable uses of force to be investigated by supervisors; and, • Use data to identify concerning trends and to identify and correct deficiencies revealed by analysis. (Please see the full agreement for exact wording and details.) a 2. Stops, Seizures, and Searches KCSO agrees to ensure that all investigatory stops, seizures, and searches are conducted in accordance with federal and state constitutions. All investigatory stops will be adequately documented for tracking and supervision purposes. KCSO shall provide training on bias-free policing and implement additional accountability and supervision practices to ensure that unlawful stops, searches, and seizures are detected and effectively addressed. KCSO will work with the Monitor on a semiannual basis to analyze its stop data and revise policies and trainings as warranted. (Please see the full agreement for exact wording and details.) a 3. Responding to and Interacting With People With Behavioral Health Disparities or in Crisis KCSO shall revise its policies to establish that deputies who are specifically trained in de-escalation techniques be dispatched to respond to calls involving a person in mental health crisis or suffering from a mental health disability. KCSO shall ensure deputies are equipped with methods to properly interact with this community, to reduce the number of individuals with behavioral health disabilities in the criminal justice system. (Please see the full agreement for exact wording and details.) a 4. Management and Supervisory Oversight KCSO will ensure all supervisors and managers exercise oversight of use of force incidents, conduct impartial investigations of those matters, are held accountable for meeting agency standards and expectations, engage with and listen to community feedback, and incorporate said feedback when able and appropriate. KCSO will develop specific metrics and guidelines for evaluating the effectiveness of the supervision of deputies and perform these evaluations annually. (Please see the full agreement for exact wording and details.) a 5. Language Access KCSO will ensure that all members of the Kern County community, regardless of their ability to speak, read, write, or understand English, will be provided with timely and meaningful access to police services and with effective communication. KCSO agrees to partner with the CAC and community stakeholders to develop and implement a language access policy consistent with applicable federal and state laws. KCSO will develop and audit protocol to determine how it is managing language access services and whether the services align with community needs. Audit results will be reported annually to the public. (Please see the full agreement for exact wording and details.) a 6. Recruitment, Hiring, and Promotions KCSO will develop and implement plans and policies to ensure it successfully attracts and hires a diverse group of qualified individuals for both patrol and detentions. These shall be designed to ensure that recruitment, hiring, and promotion decisions are made without favoritism or unlawful discrimination and incorporate enhanced strategies for promoting qualified applicant representatives of the Kern County community. KCSO will report annually on their promotional activities and outcomes. (Please see the full agreement for exact wording and details.) a 7. Community Policing KCSO agrees to enhance, promote, and strengthen partnerships within the community, to engage constructively with the community to ensure collaborative problem-solving and bias-free policing, and to increase transparency and community confidence in KCSO. To do this, KCSO will:• Develop identified policies with input from the CAC and other community stakeholders;• Create easy points of access for community feedback and input;• Develop a plan to actively attend community meetings and events;• Provide annual training on community policing and problem-oriented policing methods;• Report annually on its community engagement efforts; and,• Conduct a Community Survey with the assistance of the Monitoring Team. (Please see the full agreement for exact wording and details.) a 8. Personnel Complaint Review KCSO will ensure that all allegations of personnel misconduct are received and fully and fairly investigated. Personnel who commit misconduct will be held accountable pursuant to a fair disciplinary system and consistent standards. All KCSO deputies and supervisors will receive training about proper complaint intake, classification, and investigative techniques. Audits of these practices will be conducted annually. (Please see the full agreement for exact wording and details.)         <div class="col-lg-8" id="biography-division">
            <h1>Donny Youngblood</h1>
            <h3>Sheriff / Coroner / Public Administrator</h3>
            <p>
                In 2006, following a campaign fought on the issues of leadership and experience, the citizens of Kern County elected Donny Youngblood to the Offices of Sheriff-Coroner-Public Administrator.
                <button class="btn-green" id="biography_expand">For full biography click here.</button>
            </p>
            <p id="biography_paragraph">
                Sheriff Donny Youngblood is a life-long native of Kern County. He attended East and West High Schools, and graduated from Bakersfield College.<br>
                <br>

                He enlisted in the United States Army in 1968, serving 14 months in South Vietnam. Following his return stateside, he spent his last year in the military as an Army Drill Sergeant preparing young men to defend the United States of America. He left the military service in 1971.<br>
                <br>

                Sheriff Youngblood joined the Kern County Sheriff’s Office in 1972 as a Correctional Officer assigned to the Lerdo Facility. Two years later, he entered the Basic Academy to begin training to become a Deputy Sheriff.
                <br>
                <br>

                During his career of over 45 years with the Sheriff’s Office, Sheriff Youngblood worked in all areas of the department. His duty assignments included the Patrol Division, Court Services, Narcotics, Boron Substation, East Kern Substations Commander, Watch Commander, Air Support Division Commander, and Detectives.<br>
                <br>

                Sheriff Youngblood obtained a Bachelor of Arts Degree in Administration of Justice and a Master’s Degree in Public Administration from Golden Gate University. He is an alumnus of the 144th class of the FBI National Academy, and is also a graduate of the POST Command College.<br>
                <br>

                Sheriff Youngblood holds a commercial pilot’s license with instrument and multi-engine ratings. He is also an avid golfer, hunter and horseman.<br>
                <br>
                <button class="btn-green" id="biography_collapse">Hide full biography.</button>
            </p>

            Donny Youngblood
            Sheriff / Coroner / Public Administrator
            
                In 2006, following a campaign fought on the issues of leadership and experience, the citizens of Kern County elected Donny Youngblood to the Offices of Sheriff-Coroner-Public Administrator.
                For full biography click here.
            
            
                Sheriff Donny Youngblood is a life-long native of Kern County. He attended East and West High Schools, and graduated from Bakersfield College.
                

                He enlisted in the United States Army in 1968, serving 14 months in South Vietnam. Following his return stateside, he spent his last year in the military as an Army Drill Sergeant preparing young men to defend the United States of America. He left the military service in 1971.
                

                Sheriff Youngblood joined the Kern County Sheriff’s Office in 1972 as a Correctional Officer assigned to the Lerdo Facility. Two years later, he entered the Basic Academy to begin training to become a Deputy Sheriff.
                
                

                During his career of over 45 years with the Sheriff’s Office, Sheriff Youngblood worked in all areas of the department. His duty assignments included the Patrol Division, Court Services, Narcotics, Boron Substation, East Kern Substations Commander, Watch Commander, Air Support Division Commander, and Detectives.
                

                Sheriff Youngblood obtained a Bachelor of Arts Degree in Administration of Justice and a Master’s Degree in Public Administration from Golden Gate University. He is an alumnus of the 144th class of the FBI National Academy, and is also a graduate of the POST Command College.
                

                Sheriff Youngblood holds a commercial pilot’s license with instrument and multi-engine ratings. He is also an avid golfer, hunter and horseman.

<div class="wp-block-coblocks-accordion">
<div class="wp-block-coblocks-accordion-item"><details><summary class="wp-block-coblocks-accordion-item__title has-background has-text-color has-white-color" style="background-color:#006e8d">What is the role of the Monitors</summary><div class="wp-block-coblocks-accordion-item__content" style="border-color:#006e8d">
<p>The Monitors are a neutral third-party appointed by the court to oversee and assess KCSO and the County’s progress in implementing, and achieving compliance with, the Stipulated Judgment. They report the status of implementation to the Parties and the Court and work with the Parties to address any barriers to compliance, as well as assist the Parties to informally resolve disputes or differences should they emerge. The Monitors shall not, and are not intended to, replace or assume the role and duties of the Sheriff or of the DOJ.</p>
</div></details></div>



<div class="wp-block-coblocks-accordion-item"><details><summary class="wp-block-coblocks-accordion-item__title has-background has-text-color has-white-color" style="background-color:#006e8d">How can I contact the Monitors with a question or concern?</summary><div class="wp-block-coblocks-accordion-item__content" style="border-color:#006e8d">
<p>Inquiries and concerns can be sent to the monitors from the <a href="https://kcsomonitoring.info/about-kcso-monitoring/contact-the-monitors/">Contact the Monitors</a> page.</p>
</div></details></div>



<div class="wp-block-coblocks-accordion-item"><details><summary class="wp-block-coblocks-accordion-item__title has-background has-text-color has-white-color" style="background-color:#006e8d">How do I make an inquiry or send a question to the Sheriff’s Office?</summary><div class="wp-block-coblocks-accordion-item__content" style="border-color:#006e8d">
<p>Inquiries and questions can be sent to the Kern County Sheriff’s Office <a href="https://www.kernsheriff.org/Contact">here</a>.</p>
</div></details></div>



<div class="wp-block-coblocks-accordion-item"><details><summary class="wp-block-coblocks-accordion-item__title has-background has-text-color has-white-color" style="background-color:#006e8d">How do I share a comment or complaint about the Sheriff’s Office?</summary><div class="wp-block-coblocks-accordion-item__content" style="border-color:#006e8d">
<p>Comments and complaints regarding the Sheriff’s Office need to be submitted directly to KCSO on a Complaint Form.</p>



<p>This can be done in person at a station, at various community locations such as public libraries, or online.</p>



<p>For more information, click on the following links:</p>



<p><a href="https://www.kernsheriff.org/Internal_Affairs" target="_blank" rel="noreferrer noopener">Internal Affairs | KCSO (kernsheriff.org)</a></p>



<p><a href="https://www.kernsheriff.org/Complaints_Document/citizen_complaint_brochure.pdf" target="_blank" rel="noreferrer noopener">Document/citizen_complaint_brochure.pdf</a></p>



<p><a href="https://www.kernsheriff.org/Complaints_Document/Public_Complaint_Brochure-August_2023.pdf" target="_blank" rel="noreferrer noopener">Online personnel complaint form in English</a></p>



<p><a href="https://www.kernsheriff.org/Complaints_Document/Public%20Complaint%20Brochure.ES.pdf" target="_blank" rel="noreferrer noopener">Online personnel complaint form in Spanish</a></p>



<p><a href="https://www.kernsheriff.org/complaints" target="_blank" rel="noreferrer noopener">Process on How to Submit a Complaint</a></p>
</div></details></div>



<div class="wp-block-coblocks-accordion-item"><details><summary class="wp-block-coblocks-accordion-item__title has-background has-text-color has-white-color" style="background-color:#006e8d">What is the Communitywide Advisory Council (CAC) and how can I learn more about it?</summary><div class="wp-block-coblocks-accordion-item__content" style="border-color:#006e8d">
<p>The KCSO Communitywide Advisory Council (CAC) was established as part of the stipulated judgment. The CAC is a diverse group of Kern County residents advocating for positive change in relations, policies, and laws to create a safer community. CAC meetings are open to the public (see the <a href="https://kcsomonitoring.info/news-events/">News & Events</a> page) via Zoom, and focus on the eight key areas of reforms and objectives to be met by KCSO, as identified in the stipulated judgment. To learn more about the CAC, visit <a href="https://kerncac.org/" target="_blank" rel="noreferrer noopener">https://kerncac.org</a>.</p>
</div></details></div>



<div class="wp-block-coblocks-accordion-item"><details><summary class="wp-block-coblocks-accordion-item__title has-background has-text-color has-white-color" style="background-color:#006e8d">How do I submit a complaint against the County of Kern?</summary><div class="wp-block-coblocks-accordion-item__content" style="border-color:#006e8d">

<h4>The Stipulated Judgment</h4>
<p>The Stipulated Judgment specifically identifies eight key areas of reforms and objectives to be met by KCSO, which are briefly summarized here. Please see the <a href="https://oag.ca.gov/sites/default/files/Judgment.pdf" data-type="URL" data-id="https://oag.ca.gov/sites/default/files/Judgment.pdf">full judgment</a> for exact wording and details.</p>
<div class="ewd-ufaq-faq-list ewd-ufaq-page-type-distinct ewd-ufaq-category-tabs-" id="ewd-ufaq-faq-list">
<p>	<input type="hidden" name="show_on_load" value="" id="ewd-ufaq-show-on-load"><br>
<input type="hidden" name="include_category" value="" id="ewd-ufaq-include-category"><br>

<input type="hidden" name="current_url" value="/" id="ewd-ufaq-current-url"></p>
<div class="ewd-ufaq-faqs">
<div id="ewd-ufaq-faq-category-judgement-details" class="ewd-ufaq-faq-category">
<div class="ewd-ufaq-faq-category-title ">
<h3 title="Click here to open Key Judgment Sections">
			Key Judgment Sections					</h3>
<p></p></div>
<div class="ewd-ufaq-faq-category-inner ">
<div class="ewd-ufaq-faq-div ewd-ufaq-faq-column-count-one ewd-ufaq-faq-responsive-columns- ewd-ufaq-faq-display-style-default ewd-ufaq-can-be-toggled" id="ewd-ufaq-post-137-cX64ds5AMI" data-post_id="137">
<div class="ewd-ufaq-faq-title ewd-ufaq-faq-toggle">
<p>	<a class="ewd-ufaq-post-margin" href="#" role="button"></a></p><a class="ewd-ufaq-post-margin" href="#" role="button">
<div class="ewd-ufaq-post-margin-symbol ewd-ufaq-">
			<span>a</span>
		</div>
<div class="ewd-ufaq-faq-title-text">
<h4>
				1. Use of Force			</h4>
<p></p></div>
<div class="ewd-ufaq-clear"></div>
</a><p><a class="ewd-ufaq-post-margin" href="#" role="button">	</a></p>
</div>
<div class="ewd-ufaq-faq-body ewd-ufaq-hidden">
<div class="ewd-ufaq-post-margin ewd-ufaq-faq-post">
<p>KCSO agrees to revise its use of force policies and practices in accordance with both federal and state constitutions; federal and state laws; and to include the concepts of sanctity of life, necessity, proportionality, and de-escalation. Deputies shall receive training on all new and updated policies. KCSO deputies and staff will use force only when necessary to defend against an imminent threat of death or serious bodily injury; when feasible, they will use de-escalation techniques, crisis intervention tactics, and other alternatives. The KCSO shall:</p>
<p>• Have an affirmative duty to intervene when another deputy/employee is about to use, or is using, unnecessary or excessive force;<br>• Require deputies to report all uses of force greater than an authorized control hold;<br>• Develop a strategic plan to meaningfully engage with the community and work with the CAC in developing the revised use of force policies;<br>• Develop a policy and process to inform the public about all officer involved shootings, deaths in custody;<br>• Prohibit chokeholds, carotid restrains, and other such maneuvers;<br>• Revise its canine-related policies and training;<br>• Mandate reportable uses of force to be investigated by supervisors; and, <br>• Use data to identify concerning trends and to identify and correct deficiencies revealed by analysis.</p>
<p>(Please see the <a href="https://oag.ca.gov/sites/default/files/Judgment.pdf">full agreement</a> for exact wording and details.)</p>
</div></div>
</div>
<div class="ewd-ufaq-faq-div ewd-ufaq-faq-column-count-one ewd-ufaq-faq-responsive-columns- ewd-ufaq-faq-display-style-default ewd-ufaq-can-be-toggled" id="ewd-ufaq-post-136-bRleAGBArI" data-post_id="136">
<div class="ewd-ufaq-faq-title ewd-ufaq-faq-toggle">
<p>	<a class="ewd-ufaq-post-margin" href="#" role="button"></a></p><a class="ewd-ufaq-post-margin" href="#" role="button">
<div class="ewd-ufaq-post-margin-symbol ewd-ufaq-">
			<span>a</span>
		</div>
<div class="ewd-ufaq-faq-title-text">
<h4>
				2. Stops, Seizures, and Searches			</h4>
<p></p></div>
<div class="ewd-ufaq-clear"></div>
</a><p><a class="ewd-ufaq-post-margin" href="#" role="button">	</a></p>
</div>
<div class="ewd-ufaq-faq-body ewd-ufaq-hidden">
<div class="ewd-ufaq-post-margin ewd-ufaq-faq-post">
<p>KCSO agrees to ensure that all investigatory stops, seizures, and searches are conducted in accordance with federal and state constitutions. All investigatory stops will be adequately documented for tracking and supervision purposes. KCSO shall provide training on bias-free policing and implement additional accountability and supervision practices to ensure that unlawful stops, searches, and seizures are detected and effectively addressed. KCSO will work with the Monitor on a semiannual basis to analyze its stop data and revise policies and trainings as warranted.</p>
<p>(Please see the <a href="https://oag.ca.gov/sites/default/files/Judgment.pdf">full agreement</a> for exact wording and details.)</p>
<p></p>
</div></div>
</div>
<div class="ewd-ufaq-faq-div ewd-ufaq-faq-column-count-one ewd-ufaq-faq-responsive-columns- ewd-ufaq-faq-display-style-default ewd-ufaq-can-be-toggled" id="ewd-ufaq-post-193-yyvGODlZDz" data-post_id="193">
<div class="ewd-ufaq-faq-title ewd-ufaq-faq-toggle">
<p>	<a class="ewd-ufaq-post-margin" href="#" role="button"></a></p><a class="ewd-ufaq-post-margin" href="#" role="button">
<div class="ewd-ufaq-post-margin-symbol ewd-ufaq-">
			<span>a</span>
		</div>
<div class="ewd-ufaq-faq-title-text">
<h4>
				3. Responding to and Interacting With People With Behavioral Health Disparities or in Crisis			</h4>
<p></p></div>
<div class="ewd-ufaq-clear"></div>
</a><p><a class="ewd-ufaq-post-margin" href="#" role="button">	</a></p>
</div>
<div class="ewd-ufaq-faq-body ewd-ufaq-hidden">
<div class="ewd-ufaq-post-margin ewd-ufaq-faq-post">
<p>KCSO shall revise its policies to establish that deputies who are specifically trained in de-escalation techniques be dispatched to respond to calls involving a person in mental health crisis or suffering from a mental health disability. KCSO shall ensure deputies are equipped with methods to properly interact with this community, to reduce the number of individuals with behavioral health disabilities in the criminal justice system.</p>
<p>(Please see the <a href="https://oag.ca.gov/sites/default/files/Judgment.pdf">full agreement</a> for exact wording and details.)</p>
</div></div>
</div>
<div class="ewd-ufaq-faq-div ewd-ufaq-faq-column-count-one ewd-ufaq-faq-responsive-columns- ewd-ufaq-faq-display-style-default ewd-ufaq-can-be-toggled" id="ewd-ufaq-post-194-hBfXGURwtY" data-post_id="194">
<div class="ewd-ufaq-faq-title ewd-ufaq-faq-toggle">
<p>	<a class="ewd-ufaq-post-margin" href="#" role="button"></a></p><a class="ewd-ufaq-post-margin" href="#" role="button">
<div class="ewd-ufaq-post-margin-symbol ewd-ufaq-">
			<span>a</span>
		</div>
<div class="ewd-ufaq-faq-title-text">
<h4>
				4. Management and Supervisory Oversight			</h4>
<p></p></div>
<div class="ewd-ufaq-clear"></div>
</a><p><a class="ewd-ufaq-post-margin" href="#" role="button">	</a></p>
</div>
<div class="ewd-ufaq-faq-body ewd-ufaq-hidden">
<div class="ewd-ufaq-post-margin ewd-ufaq-faq-post">
<p>KCSO will ensure all supervisors and managers exercise oversight of use of force incidents, conduct impartial investigations of those matters, are held accountable for meeting agency standards and expectations, engage with and listen to community feedback, and incorporate said feedback when able and appropriate. KCSO will develop specific metrics and guidelines for evaluating the effectiveness of the supervision of deputies and perform these evaluations annually.</p>
<p>(Please see the <a href="https://oag.ca.gov/sites/default/files/Judgment.pdf">full agreement</a> for exact wording and details.)</p>
</div></div>
</div>
<div class="ewd-ufaq-faq-div ewd-ufaq-faq-column-count-one ewd-ufaq-faq-responsive-columns- ewd-ufaq-faq-display-style-default ewd-ufaq-can-be-toggled" id="ewd-ufaq-post-195-PicM8MjIPK" data-post_id="195">
<div class="ewd-ufaq-faq-title ewd-ufaq-faq-toggle">
<p>	<a class="ewd-ufaq-post-margin" href="#" role="button"></a></p><a class="ewd-ufaq-post-margin" href="#" role="button">
<div class="ewd-ufaq-post-margin-symbol ewd-ufaq-">
			<span>a</span>
		</div>
<div class="ewd-ufaq-faq-title-text">
<h4>
				5. Language Access			</h4>
<p></p></div>
<div class="ewd-ufaq-clear"></div>
</a><p><a class="ewd-ufaq-post-margin" href="#" role="button">	</a></p>
</div>
<div class="ewd-ufaq-faq-body ewd-ufaq-hidden">
<div class="ewd-ufaq-post-margin ewd-ufaq-faq-post">
<p>KCSO will ensure that all members of the Kern County community, regardless of their ability to speak, read, write, or understand English, will be provided with timely and meaningful access to police services and with effective communication. KCSO agrees to partner with the CAC and community stakeholders to develop and implement a language access policy consistent with applicable federal and state laws. KCSO will develop and audit protocol to determine how it is managing language access services and whether the services align with community needs. Audit results will be reported annually to the public.</p>
<p>(Please see the <a href="https://oag.ca.gov/sites/default/files/Judgment.pdf">full agreement</a> for exact wording and details.)</p>
</div></div>
</div>
<div class="ewd-ufaq-faq-div ewd-ufaq-faq-column-count-one ewd-ufaq-faq-responsive-columns- ewd-ufaq-faq-display-style-default ewd-ufaq-can-be-toggled" id="ewd-ufaq-post-196-hd2bdKOrsD" data-post_id="196">
<div class="ewd-ufaq-faq-title ewd-ufaq-faq-toggle">
<p>	<a class="ewd-ufaq-post-margin" href="#" role="button"></a></p><a class="ewd-ufaq-post-margin" href="#" role="button">
<div class="ewd-ufaq-post-margin-symbol ewd-ufaq-">
			<span>a</span>
		</div>
<div class="ewd-ufaq-faq-title-text">
<h4>
				6. Recruitment, Hiring, and Promotions			</h4>
<p></p></div>
<div class="ewd-ufaq-clear"></div>
</a><p><a class="ewd-ufaq-post-margin" href="#" role="button">	</a></p>
</div>
<div class="ewd-ufaq-faq-body ewd-ufaq-hidden">
<div class="ewd-ufaq-post-margin ewd-ufaq-faq-post">
<p>KCSO will develop and implement plans and policies to ensure it successfully attracts and hires a diverse group of qualified individuals for both patrol and detentions. These shall be designed to ensure that recruitment, hiring, and promotion decisions are made without favoritism or unlawful discrimination and incorporate enhanced strategies for promoting qualified applicant representatives of the Kern County community. KCSO will report annually on their promotional activities and outcomes.</p>
<p>(Please see the <a href="https://oag.ca.gov/sites/default/files/Judgment.pdf">full agreement</a> for exact wording and details.)</p>
</div></div>
</div>
<div class="ewd-ufaq-faq-div ewd-ufaq-faq-column-count-one ewd-ufaq-faq-responsive-columns- ewd-ufaq-faq-display-style-default ewd-ufaq-can-be-toggled" id="ewd-ufaq-post-197-8qpli8hSKz" data-post_id="197">
<div class="ewd-ufaq-faq-title ewd-ufaq-faq-toggle">
<p>	<a class="ewd-ufaq-post-margin" href="#" role="button"></a></p><a class="ewd-ufaq-post-margin" href="#" role="button">
<div class="ewd-ufaq-post-margin-symbol ewd-ufaq-">
			<span>a</span>
		</div>
<div class="ewd-ufaq-faq-title-text">
<h4>
				7. Community Policing			</h4>
<p></p></div>
<div class="ewd-ufaq-clear"></div>
</a><p><a class="ewd-ufaq-post-margin" href="#" role="button">	</a></p>
</div>
<div class="ewd-ufaq-faq-body ewd-ufaq-hidden">
<div class="ewd-ufaq-post-margin ewd-ufaq-faq-post">
<p>KCSO agrees to enhance, promote, and strengthen partnerships within the community, to engage constructively with the community to ensure collaborative problem-solving and bias-free policing, and to increase transparency and community confidence in KCSO. To do this, KCSO will:<br>• Develop identified policies with input from the CAC and other community stakeholders;<br>• Create easy points of access for community feedback and input;<br>• Develop a plan to actively attend community meetings and events;<br>• Provide annual training on community policing and problem-oriented policing methods;<br>• Report annually on its community engagement efforts; and,<br>• Conduct a Community Survey with the assistance of the Monitoring Team.</p>
<p>(Please see the <a href="https://oag.ca.gov/sites/default/files/Judgment.pdf">full agreement</a> for exact wording and details.)</p>
</div></div>
</div>
<div class="ewd-ufaq-faq-div ewd-ufaq-faq-column-count-one ewd-ufaq-faq-responsive-columns- ewd-ufaq-faq-display-style-default ewd-ufaq-can-be-toggled" id="ewd-ufaq-post-198-RcBuyUwleG" data-post_id="198">
<div class="ewd-ufaq-faq-title ewd-ufaq-faq-toggle">
<p>	<a class="ewd-ufaq-post-margin" href="#" role="button"></a></p><a class="ewd-ufaq-post-margin" href="#" role="button">
<div class="ewd-ufaq-post-margin-symbol ewd-ufaq-">
			<span>a</span>
		</div>
<div class="ewd-ufaq-faq-title-text">
<h4>
				8. Personnel Complaint Review			</h4>
<p></p></div>
<div class="ewd-ufaq-clear"></div>
</a><p><a class="ewd-ufaq-post-margin" href="#" role="button">	</a></p>
</div>
<div class="ewd-ufaq-faq-body ewd-ufaq-hidden">
<div class="ewd-ufaq-post-margin ewd-ufaq-faq-post">
<p>KCSO will ensure that all allegations of personnel misconduct are received and fully and fairly investigated. Personnel who commit misconduct will be held accountable pursuant to a fair disciplinary system and consistent standards. All KCSO deputies and supervisors will receive training about proper complaint intake, classification, and investigative techniques. Audits of these practices will be conducted annually.</p>
<p>(Please see the <a href="https://oag.ca.gov/sites/default/files/Judgment.pdf" target="_blank" rel="noreferrer noopener">full agreement</a> for exact wording and details.)</p>
</div></div>
</div>

FAQs What is the role of the Monitors The Monitors are a neutral third-party appointed by the court to oversee and assess KCSO and the County’s progress in implementing, and achieving compliance with, the Stipulated Judgment. They report the status of implementation to the Parties and the Court and work with the Parties to address any barriers to compliance, as well as assist the Parties to informally resolve disputes or differences should they emerge. The Monitors shall not, and are not intended to, replace or assume the role and duties of the Sheriff or of the DOJ. How can I contact the Monitors with a question or concern? Inquiries and concerns can be sent to the monitors from the Contact the Monitors page. How do I make an inquiry or send a question to the Sheriff’s Office? Inquiries and questions can be sent to the Kern County Sheriff’s Office here. How do I share a comment or complaint about the Sheriff’s Office? Comments and complaints regarding the Sheriff’s Office need to be submitted directly to KCSO on a Complaint Form. This can be done in person at a station, at various community locations such as public libraries, or online. For more information, click on the following links: Internal Affairs | KCSO (kernsheriff.org) Document/citizen_complaint_brochure.pdf Online personnel complaint form in English Online personnel complaint form in Spanish Process on How to Submit a Complaint What is the Communitywide Advisory Council (CAC) and how can I learn more about it? The KCSO Communitywide Advisory Council (CAC) was established as part of the stipulated judgment. The CAC is a diverse group of Kern County residents advocating for positive change in relations, policies, and laws to create a safer community. CAC meetings are open to the public (see the News & Events page) via Zoom, and focus on the eight key areas of reforms and objectives to be met by KCSO, as identified in the stipulated judgment. To learn more about the CAC, visit https://kerncac.org. How do I submit a complaint against the County of Kern? Claim Against the County of Kern Important Links  Kern County Sheriff’s OfficeTransparency | KCSO (kernsheriff.org)Kern County, CAState of California, Department of Justice The Stipulated Judgment The Stipulated Judgment specifically identifies eight key areas of reforms and objectives to be met by KCSO, which are briefly summarized here. Please see the full judgment for exact wording and details. Key Judgment Sections a 1. Use of Force KCSO agrees to revise its use of force policies and practices in accordance with both federal and state constitutions; federal and state laws; and to include the concepts of sanctity of life, necessity, proportionality, and de-escalation. Deputies shall receive training on all new and updated policies. KCSO deputies and staff will use force only when necessary to defend against an imminent threat of death or serious bodily injury; when feasible, they will use de-escalation techniques, crisis intervention tactics, and other alternatives. The KCSO shall: • Have an affirmative duty to intervene when another deputy/employee is about to use, or is using, unnecessary or excessive force;• Require deputies to report all uses of force greater than an authorized control hold;• Develop a strategic plan to meaningfully engage with the community and work with the CAC in developing the revised use of force policies;• Develop a policy and process to inform the public about all officer involved shootings, deaths in custody;• Prohibit chokeholds, carotid restrains, and other such maneuvers;• Revise its canine-related policies and training;• Mandate reportable uses of force to be investigated by supervisors; and, • Use data to identify concerning trends and to identify and correct deficiencies revealed by analysis. (Please see the full agreement for exact wording and details.) a 2. Stops, Seizures, and Searches KCSO agrees to ensure that all investigatory stops, seizures, and searches are conducted in accordance with federal and state constitutions. All investigatory stops will be adequately documented for tracking and supervision purposes. KCSO shall provide training on bias-free policing and implement additional accountability and supervision practices to ensure that unlawful stops, searches, and seizures are detected and effectively addressed. KCSO will work with the Monitor on a semiannual basis to analyze its stop data and revise policies and trainings as warranted. (Please see the full agreement for exact wording and details.) a 3. Responding to and Interacting With People With Behavioral Health Disparities or in Crisis KCSO shall revise its policies to establish that deputies who are specifically trained in de-escalation techniques be dispatched to respond to calls involving a person in mental health crisis or suffering from a mental health disability. KCSO shall ensure deputies are equipped with methods to properly interact with this community, to reduce the number of individuals with behavioral health disabilities in the criminal justice system. (Please see the full agreement for exact wording and details.) a 4. Management and Supervisory Oversight KCSO will ensure all supervisors and managers exercise oversight of use of force incidents, conduct impartial investigations of those matters, are held accountable for meeting agency standards and expectations, engage with and listen to community feedback, and incorporate said feedback when able and appropriate. KCSO will develop specific metrics and guidelines for evaluating the effectiveness of the supervision of deputies and perform these evaluations annually. (Please see the full agreement for exact wording and details.) a 5. Language Access KCSO will ensure that all members of the Kern County community, regardless of their ability to speak, read, write, or understand English, will be provided with timely and meaningful access to police services and with effective communication. KCSO agrees to partner with the CAC and community stakeholders to develop and implement a language access policy consistent with applicable federal and state laws. KCSO will develop and audit protocol to determine how it is managing language access services and whether the services align with community needs. Audit results will be reported annually to the public. (Please see the full agreement for exact wording and details.) a 6. Recruitment, Hiring, and Promotions KCSO will develop and implement plans and policies to ensure it successfully attracts and hires a diverse group of qualified individuals for both patrol and detentions. These shall be designed to ensure that recruitment, hiring, and promotion decisions are made without favoritism or unlawful discrimination and incorporate enhanced strategies for promoting qualified applicant representatives of the Kern County community. KCSO will report annually on their promotional activities and outcomes. (Please see the full agreement for exact wording and details.) a 7. Community Policing KCSO agrees to enhance, promote, and strengthen partnerships within the community, to engage constructively with the community to ensure collaborative problem-solving and bias-free policing, and to increase transparency and community confidence in KCSO. To do this, KCSO will:• Develop identified policies with input from the CAC and other community stakeholders;• Create easy points of access for community feedback and input;• Develop a plan to actively attend community meetings and events;• Provide annual training on community policing and problem-oriented policing methods;• Report annually on its community engagement efforts; and,• Conduct a Community Survey with the assistance of the Monitoring Team. (Please see the full agreement for exact wording and details.) a 8. Personnel Complaint Review KCSO will ensure that all allegations of personnel misconduct are received and fully and fairly investigated. Personnel who commit misconduct will be held accountable pursuant to a fair disciplinary system and consistent standards. All KCSO deputies and supervisors will receive training about proper complaint intake, classification, and investigative techniques. Audits of these practices will be conducted annually. (Please see the full agreement for exact wording and details.) 				  <h4>FAQs</h4>
				  
<div class="wp-block-coblocks-accordion">
<div class="wp-block-coblocks-accordion-item"><details><summary class="wp-block-coblocks-accordion-item__title has-background has-text-color has-white-color" style="background-color:#006e8d">What is the role of the Monitors</summary><div class="wp-block-coblocks-accordion-item__content" style="border-color:#006e8d">
<p>The Monitors are a neutral third-party appointed by the court to oversee and assess KCSO and the County’s progress in implementing, and achieving compliance with, the Stipulated Judgment. They report the status of implementation to the Parties and the Court and work with the Parties to address any barriers to compliance, as well as assist the Parties to informally resolve disputes or differences should they emerge. The Monitors shall not, and are not intended to, replace or assume the role and duties of the Sheriff or of the DOJ.</p>
</div></details></div>



<div class="wp-block-coblocks-accordion-item"><details><summary class="wp-block-coblocks-accordion-item__title has-background has-text-color has-white-color" style="background-color:#006e8d">How can I contact the Monitors with a question or concern?</summary><div class="wp-block-coblocks-accordion-item__content" style="border-color:#006e8d">
<p>Inquiries and concerns can be sent to the monitors from the <a href="https://kcsomonitoring.info/about-kcso-monitoring/contact-the-monitors/">Contact the Monitors</a> page.</p>
</div></details></div>



<div class="wp-block-coblocks-accordion-item"><details><summary class="wp-block-coblocks-accordion-item__title has-background has-text-color has-white-color" style="background-color:#006e8d">How do I make an inquiry or send a question to the Sheriff’s Office?</summary><div class="wp-block-coblocks-accordion-item__content" style="border-color:#006e8d">
<p>Inquiries and questions can be sent to the Kern County Sheriff’s Office <a href="https://www.kernsheriff.org/Contact">here</a>.</p>
</div></details></div>



<div class="wp-block-coblocks-accordion-item"><details><summary class="wp-block-coblocks-accordion-item__title has-background has-text-color has-white-color" style="background-color:#006e8d">How do I share a comment or complaint about the Sheriff’s Office?</summary><div class="wp-block-coblocks-accordion-item__content" style="border-color:#006e8d">
<p>Comments and complaints regarding the Sheriff’s Office need to be submitted directly to KCSO on a Complaint Form.</p>



<p>This can be done in person at a station, at various community locations such as public libraries, or online.</p>



<p>For more information, click on the following links:</p>



<p><a href="https://www.kernsheriff.org/Internal_Affairs" target="_blank" rel="noreferrer noopener">Internal Affairs | KCSO (kernsheriff.org)</a></p>



<p><a href="https://www.kernsheriff.org/Complaints_Document/citizen_complaint_brochure.pdf" target="_blank" rel="noreferrer noopener">Document/citizen_complaint_brochure.pdf</a></p>



<p><a href="https://www.kernsheriff.org/Complaints_Document/Public_Complaint_Brochure-August_2023.pdf" target="_blank" rel="noreferrer noopener">Online personnel complaint form in English</a></p>



<p><a href="https://www.kernsheriff.org/Complaints_Document/Public%20Complaint%20Brochure.ES.pdf" target="_blank" rel="noreferrer noopener">Online personnel complaint form in Spanish</a></p>



<p><a href="https://www.kernsheriff.org/complaints" target="_blank" rel="noreferrer noopener">Process on How to Submit a Complaint</a></p>
</div></details></div>



<div class="wp-block-coblocks-accordion-item"><details><summary class="wp-block-coblocks-accordion-item__title has-background has-text-color has-white-color" style="background-color:#006e8d">What is the Communitywide Advisory Council (CAC) and how can I learn more about it?</summary><div class="wp-block-coblocks-accordion-item__content" style="border-color:#006e8d">
<p>The KCSO Communitywide Advisory Council (CAC) was established as part of the stipulated judgment. The CAC is a diverse group of Kern County residents advocating for positive change in relations, policies, and laws to create a safer community. CAC meetings are open to the public (see the <a href="https://kcsomonitoring.info/news-events/">News & Events</a> page) via Zoom, and focus on the eight key areas of reforms and objectives to be met by KCSO, as identified in the stipulated judgment. To learn more about the CAC, visit <a href="https://kerncac.org/" target="_blank" rel="noreferrer noopener">https://kerncac.org</a>.</p>
</div></details></div>



<div class="wp-block-coblocks-accordion-item"><details><summary class="wp-block-coblocks-accordion-item__title has-background has-text-color has-white-color" style="background-color:#006e8d">How do I submit a complaint against the County of Kern?</summary><div class="wp-block-coblocks-accordion-item__content" style="border-color:#006e8d">

<h4>The Stipulated Judgment</h4>
<p>The Stipulated Judgment specifically identifies eight key areas of reforms and objectives to be met by KCSO, which are briefly summarized here. Please see the <a href="https://oag.ca.gov/sites/default/files/Judgment.pdf" data-type="URL" data-id="https://oag.ca.gov/sites/default/files/Judgment.pdf">full judgment</a> for exact wording and details.</p>
<div class="ewd-ufaq-faq-list ewd-ufaq-page-type-distinct ewd-ufaq-category-tabs-" id="ewd-ufaq-faq-list">
<p>	<input type="hidden" name="show_on_load" value="" id="ewd-ufaq-show-on-load"><br>
<input type="hidden" name="include_category" value="" id="ewd-ufaq-include-category"><br>
<input type="hidden" name="exclude_category" value="" id="ewd-ufaq-exclude-category"><br>
<input type="hidden" name="orderby" value="title" id="ewd-ufaq-orderby"><br>
<input type="hidden" name="order" value="asc" id="ewd-ufaq-order"><br>
<input type="hidden" name="post_count" value="-1" id="ewd-ufaq-post-count"><br>
<input type="hidden" name="current_url" value="/" id="ewd-ufaq-current-url"></p>
<div class="ewd-ufaq-faqs">
<div id="ewd-ufaq-faq-category-judgement-details" class="ewd-ufaq-faq-category">
<div class="ewd-ufaq-faq-category-title ">
<h3 title="Click here to open Key Judgment Sections">
			Key Judgment Sections					</h3>
<p></p></div>
<div class="ewd-ufaq-faq-category-inner ">
<div class="ewd-ufaq-faq-div ewd-ufaq-faq-column-count-one ewd-ufaq-faq-responsive-columns- ewd-ufaq-faq-display-style-default ewd-ufaq-can-be-toggled" id="ewd-ufaq-post-137-cX64ds5AMI" data-post_id="137">
<div class="ewd-ufaq-faq-title ewd-ufaq-faq-toggle">
<p>	<a class="ewd-ufaq-post-margin" href="#" role="button"></a></p><a class="ewd-ufaq-post-margin" href="#" role="button">
<div class="ewd-ufaq-post-margin-symbol ewd-ufaq-">
			<span>a</span>
		</div>
<div class="ewd-ufaq-faq-title-text">
<h4>
				1. Use of Force			</h4>
<p></p></div>
<div class="ewd-ufaq-clear"></div>
</a><p><a class="ewd-ufaq-post-margin" href="#" role="button">	</a></p>
</div>
<div class="ewd-ufaq-faq-body ewd-ufaq-hidden">
<div class="ewd-ufaq-post-margin ewd-ufaq-faq-post">
<p>KCSO agrees to revise its use of force policies and practices in accordance with both federal and state constitutions; federal and state laws; and to include the concepts of sanctity of life, necessity, proportionality, and de-escalation. Deputies shall receive training on all new and updated policies. KCSO deputies and staff will use force only when necessary to defend against an imminent threat of death or serious bodily injury; when feasible, they will use de-escalation techniques, crisis intervention tactics, and other alternatives. The KCSO shall:</p>
<p>• Have an affirmative duty to intervene when another deputy/employee is about to use, or is using, unnecessary or excessive force;<br>• Require deputies to report all uses of force greater than an authorized control hold;<br>• Develop a strategic plan to meaningfully engage with the community and work with the CAC in developing the revised use of force policies;<br>• Develop a policy and process to inform the public about all officer involved shootings, deaths in custody;<br>• Prohibit chokeholds, carotid restrains, and other such maneuvers;<br>• Revise its canine-related policies and training;<br>• Mandate reportable uses of force to be investigated by supervisors; and, <br>• Use data to identify concerning trends and to identify and correct deficiencies revealed by analysis.</p>
<p>(Please see the <a href="https://oag.ca.gov/sites/default/files/Judgment.pdf">full agreement</a> for exact wording and details.)</p>
</div></div>
</div>
<div class="ewd-ufaq-faq-div ewd-ufaq-faq-column-count-one ewd-ufaq-faq-responsive-columns- ewd-ufaq-faq-display-style-default ewd-ufaq-can-be-toggled" id="ewd-ufaq-post-136-bRleAGBArI" data-post_id="136">
<div class="ewd-ufaq-faq-title ewd-ufaq-faq-toggle">
<p>	<a class="ewd-ufaq-post-margin" href="#" role="button"></a></p><a class="ewd-ufaq-post-margin" href="#" role="button">
<div class="ewd-ufaq-post-margin-symbol ewd-ufaq-">
			<span>a</span>
		</div>
<div class="ewd-ufaq-faq-title-text">
<h4>
				2. Stops, Seizures, and Searches			</h4>
<p></p></div>
<div class="ewd-ufaq-clear"></div>
</a><p><a class="ewd-ufaq-post-margin" href="#" role="button">	</a></p>
</div>
<div class="ewd-ufaq-faq-body ewd-ufaq-hidden">
<div class="ewd-ufaq-post-margin ewd-ufaq-faq-post">
<p>KCSO agrees to ensure that all investigatory stops, seizures, and searches are conducted in accordance with federal and state constitutions. All investigatory stops will be adequately documented for tracking and supervision purposes. KCSO shall provide training on bias-free policing and implement additional accountability and supervision practices to ensure that unlawful stops, searches, and seizures are detected and effectively addressed. KCSO will work with the Monitor on a semiannual basis to analyze its stop data and revise policies and trainings as warranted.</p>
<p>(Please see the <a href="https://oag.ca.gov/sites/default/files/Judgment.pdf">full agreement</a> for exact wording and details.)</p>
<p></p>
</div></div>
</div>
<div class="ewd-ufaq-faq-div ewd-ufaq-faq-column-count-one ewd-ufaq-faq-responsive-columns- ewd-ufaq-faq-display-style-default ewd-ufaq-can-be-toggled" id="ewd-ufaq-post-193-yyvGODlZDz" data-post_id="193">
<div class="ewd-ufaq-faq-title ewd-ufaq-faq-toggle">
<p>	<a class="ewd-ufaq-post-margin" href="#" role="button"></a></p><a class="ewd-ufaq-post-margin" href="#" role="button">
<div class="ewd-ufaq-post-margin-symbol ewd-ufaq-">
			<span>a</span>
		</div>
<div class="ewd-ufaq-faq-title-text">
<h4>
				3. Responding to and Interacting With People With Behavioral Health Disparities or in Crisis			</h4>
<p></p></div>
<div class="ewd-ufaq-clear"></div>
</a><p><a class="ewd-ufaq-post-margin" href="#" role="button">	</a></p>
</div>
<div class="ewd-ufaq-faq-body ewd-ufaq-hidden">
<div class="ewd-ufaq-post-margin ewd-ufaq-faq-post">
<p>KCSO shall revise its policies to establish that deputies who are specifically trained in de-escalation techniques be dispatched to respond to calls involving a person in mental health crisis or suffering from a mental health disability. KCSO shall ensure deputies are equipped with methods to properly interact with this community, to reduce the number of individuals with behavioral health disabilities in the criminal justice system.</p>
<p>(Please see the <a href="https://oag.ca.gov/sites/default/files/Judgment.pdf">full agreement</a> for exact wording and details.)</p>
</div></div>
</div>
<div class="ewd-ufaq-faq-div ewd-ufaq-faq-column-count-one ewd-ufaq-faq-responsive-columns- ewd-ufaq-faq-display-style-default ewd-ufaq-can-be-toggled" id="ewd-ufaq-post-194-hBfXGURwtY" data-post_id="194">
<div class="ewd-ufaq-faq-title ewd-ufaq-faq-toggle">
<p>	<a class="ewd-ufaq-post-margin" href="#" role="button"></a></p><a class="ewd-ufaq-post-margin" href="#" role="button">
<div class="ewd-ufaq-post-margin-symbol ewd-ufaq-">
			<span>a</span>
		</div>
<div class="ewd-ufaq-faq-title-text">
<h4>
				4. Management and Supervisory Oversight			</h4>
<p></p></div>
<div class="ewd-ufaq-clear"></div>
</a><p><a class="ewd-ufaq-post-margin" href="#" role="button">	</a></p>
</div>
<div class="ewd-ufaq-faq-body ewd-ufaq-hidden">
<div class="ewd-ufaq-post-margin ewd-ufaq-faq-post">
<p>KCSO will ensure all supervisors and managers exercise oversight of use of force incidents, conduct impartial investigations of those matters, are held accountable for meeting agency standards and expectations, engage with and listen to community feedback, and incorporate said feedback when able and appropriate. KCSO will develop specific metrics and guidelines for evaluating the effectiveness of the supervision of deputies and perform these evaluations annually.</p>
<p>(Please see the <a href="https://oag.ca.gov/sites/default/files/Judgment.pdf">full agreement</a> for exact wording and details.)</p>
</div></div>
</div>
<div class="ewd-ufaq-faq-div ewd-ufaq-faq-column-count-one ewd-ufaq-faq-responsive-columns- ewd-ufaq-faq-display-style-default ewd-ufaq-can-be-toggled" id="ewd-ufaq-post-195-PicM8MjIPK" data-post_id="195">
<div class="ewd-ufaq-faq-title ewd-ufaq-faq-toggle">
<p>	<a class="ewd-ufaq-post-margin" href="#" role="button"></a></p><a class="ewd-ufaq-post-margin" href="#" role="button">
<div class="ewd-ufaq-post-margin-symbol ewd-ufaq-">
			<span>a</span>
		</div>
<div class="ewd-ufaq-faq-title-text">
<h4>
				5. Language Access			</h4>
<p></p></div>
<div class="ewd-ufaq-clear"></div>
</a><p><a class="ewd-ufaq-post-margin" href="#" role="button">	</a></p>
</div>
<div class="ewd-ufaq-faq-body ewd-ufaq-hidden">
<div class="ewd-ufaq-post-margin ewd-ufaq-faq-post">
<p>KCSO will ensure that all members of the Kern County community, regardless of their ability to speak, read, write, or understand English, will be provided with timely and meaningful access to police services and with effective communication. KCSO agrees to partner with the CAC and community stakeholders to develop and implement a language access policy consistent with applicable federal and state laws. KCSO will develop and audit protocol to determine how it is managing language access services and whether the services align with community needs. Audit results will be reported annually to the public.</p>
<p>(Please see the <a href="https://oag.ca.gov/sites/default/files/Judgment.pdf">full agreement</a> for exact wording and details.)</p>
</div></div>
</div>
<div class="ewd-ufaq-faq-div ewd-ufaq-faq-column-count-one ewd-ufaq-faq-responsive-columns- ewd-ufaq-faq-display-style-default ewd-ufaq-can-be-toggled" id="ewd-ufaq-post-196-hd2bdKOrsD" data-post_id="196">
<div class="ewd-ufaq-faq-title ewd-ufaq-faq-toggle">
<p>	<a class="ewd-ufaq-post-margin" href="#" role="button"></a></p><a class="ewd-ufaq-post-margin" href="#" role="button">
<div class="ewd-ufaq-post-margin-symbol ewd-ufaq-">
			<span>a</span>
		</div>
<div class="ewd-ufaq-faq-title-text">
<h4>
				6. Recruitment, Hiring, and Promotions			</h4>
<p></p></div>
<div class="ewd-ufaq-clear"></div>
</a><p><a class="ewd-ufaq-post-margin" href="#" role="button">	</a></p>
</div>
<div class="ewd-ufaq-faq-body ewd-ufaq-hidden">
<div class="ewd-ufaq-post-margin ewd-ufaq-faq-post">
<p>KCSO will develop and implement plans and policies to ensure it successfully attracts and hires a diverse group of qualified individuals for both patrol and detentions. These shall be designed to ensure that recruitment, hiring, and promotion decisions are made without favoritism or unlawful discrimination and incorporate enhanced strategies for promoting qualified applicant representatives of the Kern County community. KCSO will report annually on their promotional activities and outcomes.</p>
<p>(Please see the <a href="https://oag.ca.gov/sites/default/files/Judgment.pdf">full agreement</a> for exact wording and details.)</p>
</div></div>
</div>
<div class="ewd-ufaq-faq-div ewd-ufaq-faq-column-count-one ewd-ufaq-faq-responsive-columns- ewd-ufaq-faq-display-style-default ewd-ufaq-can-be-toggled" id="ewd-ufaq-post-197-8qpli8hSKz" data-post_id="197">
<div class="ewd-ufaq-faq-title ewd-ufaq-faq-toggle">
<p>	<a class="ewd-ufaq-post-margin" href="#" role="button"></a></p><a class="ewd-ufaq-post-margin" href="#" role="button">
<div class="ewd-ufaq-post-margin-symbol ewd-ufaq-">
			<span>a</span>
		</div>
<div class="ewd-ufaq-faq-title-text">
<h4>
				7. Community Policing			</h4>
<p></p></div>
<div class="ewd-ufaq-clear"></div>
</a><p><a class="ewd-ufaq-post-margin" href="#" role="button">	</a></p>
</div>
<div class="ewd-ufaq-faq-body ewd-ufaq-hidden">
<div class="ewd-ufaq-post-margin ewd-ufaq-faq-post">
<p>KCSO agrees to enhance, promote, and strengthen partnerships within the community, to engage constructively with the community to ensure collaborative problem-solving and bias-free policing, and to increase transparency and community confidence in KCSO. To do this, KCSO will:<br>• Develop identified policies with input from the CAC and other community stakeholders;<br>• Create easy points of access for community feedback and input;<br>• Develop a plan to actively attend community meetings and events;<br>• Provide annual training on community policing and problem-oriented policing methods;<br>• Report annually on its community engagement efforts; and,<br>• Conduct a Community Survey with the assistance of the Monitoring Team.</p>
<p>(Please see the <a href="https://oag.ca.gov/sites/default/files/Judgment.pdf">full agreement</a> for exact wording and details.)</p>
</div></div>
</div>
<div class="ewd-ufaq-faq-div ewd-ufaq-faq-column-count-one ewd-ufaq-faq-responsive-columns- ewd-ufaq-faq-display-style-default ewd-ufaq-can-be-toggled" id="ewd-ufaq-post-198-RcBuyUwleG" data-post_id="198">
<div class="ewd-ufaq-faq-title ewd-ufaq-faq-toggle">
<p>	<a class="ewd-ufaq-post-margin" href="#" role="button"></a></p><a class="ewd-ufaq-post-margin" href="#" role="button">
<div class="ewd-ufaq-post-margin-symbol ewd-ufaq-">
			<span>a</span>
		</div>
<div class="ewd-ufaq-faq-title-text">
<h4>
				8. Personnel Complaint Review			</h4>
<p></p></div>
<div class="ewd-ufaq-clear"></div>
</a><p><a class="ewd-ufaq-post-margin" href="#" role="button">	</a></p>
</div>
<div class="ewd-ufaq-faq-body ewd-ufaq-hidden">
<div class="ewd-ufaq-post-margin ewd-ufaq-faq-post">
<p>KCSO will ensure that all allegations of personnel misconduct are received and fully and fairly investigated. Personnel who commit misconduct will be held accountable pursuant to a fair disciplinary system and consistent standards. All KCSO deputies and supervisors will receive training about proper complaint intake, classification, and investigative techniques. Audits of these practices will be conducted annually.</p>
<p>(Please see the <a href="https://oag.ca.gov/sites/default/files/Judgment.pdf" target="_blank" rel="noreferrer noopener">full agreement</a> for exact wording and details.)</p>
</div></div>
</div>
</div>
</div></div>
